messages.author: cb1f88e59387ebfa
messages.subject: exporting to mapQTL format
parts:
Hi All,

I am trying to use R/qtl to export some data to mapQTL format (no, it is not for me, I'd just use R/qtl). In any case, I have data for an F1/F2 (309 F2 + the 2 F1, which are the two last lines of data). I have the data in 'csv' format, and I can read it in without a single problem by doing:

dat = read.cross(format = 'csv', dir = '.', 'f1f2.csv', na.strings = 'NA', genotypes = c('AA','AC','AG','AT','CC','CG','CT','GG','GT','TT'), alleles=c('A','C','G','T'), estimate.map = FALSE)

Unfortunately when I try to export it

write.cross(dat, format = 'mapqtl', filestem = 'HB', chr = 1, digits = NULL)

I get

Error: unrecognized segregation type at marker 24319 on chromosome 1

(there is at least 1 marker R/qtl does not like in every chromosome). I suspect that I might need to specify that the last 2 individuals are the F1 male and female. Alternatively I might have to remove them... In any case I'd be obliged if you could suggest what I can do to get the export done and over with...

Cheers

Federico

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] exporting to mapQTL format
parts:
write.cross with format="mapqtl" only works for phase-known 4-way cross data.

Your call to read.cross isn't really working properly. The genotypes vector for a 4-way cross needs to be a specific list of genotype codes, corresponding to these:
1 = AC, 2 = BC, 3 = AD, 4 = BD,
5 = A = AC or AD, 6 = B = BC or BD, 7 = C = AC or BC, 8 = D = AD or BD,
9 = AC or BD, 10 = AD or BC,
11 = not AC, 12 = not BC, 13 = not AD, 14 = not BD

So the data object in R is not really what you want, and while it thinks this is a 4-way cross, R/qtl can't convert it into the MapQTL format.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] exporting to mapQTL format
parts:
Finally sat down to look at this.

The write.cross function with format="mapqtl" is currently quite restrictive, in that it can only handle certain segregation types:
1:2:3:4, 1:10;4, 1:10:11:14:4, 2:3:9, 12:13:2:3:9, 5:6, 7:8

(In the code, see https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/write.cross.mq.R#L76-L163)

So because your first marker has a single genotype "7" and otherwise 1:2:3:4, the data can't be written in mapqtl format by this function.

karl

parts:
Thanks for looking into this Karl. I thought this might be the issue. I'll just toss all incomplete markers/individual combos. 
Cheers,
John

On Friday, March 10, 2017 at 1:10:13 PM UTC-6, Karl Broman wrote:
Finally sat down to look at this.

The write.cross function with format="mapqtl" is currently quite restrictive, in that it can only handle certain segregation types:
1:2:3:4, 1:10;4, 1:10:11:14:4, 2:3:9, 12:13:2:3:9, 5:6, 7:8

(In the code, see https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/write.cross.mq.R#L76-L163)

So because your first marker has a single genotype "7" and otherwise 1:2:3:4, the data can't be written in mapqtl format by this function.

karl


> On Mar 4, 2017, at 1:20 PM, John Lovell <johnt...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> FYI - This problem comes from the data having all 4 genotypes AC, AD, BC, BD, and a few partially missing A-, B-, -C, -D.
> Since my data is mostly complete, I can get around this via:
>
> > for(chr in chrnames(cross_2write)) cross_2write$geno[[chr]]$data[cross_2write$geno[[chr]]$data>4]<-NA
>
>
> On Friday, February 24, 2017 at 5:48:53 PM UTC-6, John Lovell wrote:
> Hi Karl,
> I am dealing the the same issue as Federico:
> ...
> write.cross(bad4way, filestem = "~/Downloads/bad4way", format = "mapqtl") Error: unrecognized segregation type at marker Chr01K_1008832
> ...
> Chr01K_1008832 is the 1st marker on the 1st chromosome and has a segregation pattern with the next marker that looks like this:
> > table(g2[,1], g2[,2])  
>       1   2   3   4   7
>   1 117   1   2   0   1
>   2   3  94   0   3   0
>   3   2   1 101   4   0
>   4   0   1   1  99   0
>   5   0   0   1   0   0
>
> It seems that my genotype data is in order (I can pull together a map etc.), but clearly it isn't. I have spent a bunch of time trying to troubleshoot and can't figure it out. All markers in this population are ABxCD, phase-known with all four genotypes represented. Coding follows the read.cross guidelines, using this dictionary:
>
> matrix(c(NA,"--",
>                  1, "AC",
>                  2, "BC",
>                  3, "AD",
>                  4, "BD",
>                  5 , "A-",
>                  6 , "B-",
>                  7 , "-C",
>                  8 , "-D"), ncol = 2, byrow=T)
>
> I'm attaching an .rda file with of the 1st chromosome in case you can make some time to have a look.
> Any help is appreciated.
> John
>
>
>

> On Thursday, June 25, 2015 at 7:06:29 AM UTC-5, Karl Broman wrote:
> write.cross with format="mapqtl" only works for phase-known 4-way cross data.
>
> Your call to read.cross isn't really working properly. The genotypes vector for a 4-way cross needs to be a specific list of genotype codes, corresponding to these:
> 1 = AC, 2 = BC, 3 = AD, 4 = BD,
> 5 = A = AC or AD, 6 = B = BC or BD, 7 = C = AC or BC, 8 = D = AD or BD,
> 9 = AC or BD, 10 = AD or BC,
> 11 = not AC, 12 = not BC, 13 = not AD, 14 = not BD
>
> So the data object in R is not really what you want, and while it thinks this is a 4-way cross, R/qtl can't convert it into the MapQTL format.
>
> karl
>
> > On Jun 25, 2015, at 3:27 AM, Federico Calboli <f.ca...@gmail.com> wrote:
> >

> >
> > Unfortunately when I try to export it

> > write.cross(dat, format = 'mapqtl', filestem = 'HB', chr = 1, digits = NULL)
> >

> > Error: unrecognized segregation type at marker 24319 on chromosome 1
> >
> > (there is at least 1 marker R/qtl does not like in every chromosome). I suspect that I might need to specify that the last 2 individuals are the F1 male and female. Alternatively I might have to remove them... In any case I'd be obliged if you could suggest what I can do to get the export done and over with...
